mainEntity.name: How much does a Vauxhall Corsa 1.2 PureTech engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A Vauxhall Corsa 1.2 PureTech engine replacement typically costs £1,500-£2,800 supply-only for a rebuilt unit (EB2ADTS / EB2DTS), with used engines from £400-£900. Fitting adds approximately £390-£585 in labour (6-9 hours at independent specialist rates). Main dealer fitted prices are typically 30-50% higher. Remanufactured units from specialists like Ivor Searle cost up to 40% less than OE and come with a 12-month unlimited mileage parts and labour warranty.

mainEntity.name: How much does a Vauxhall Corsa 1.5 BlueHDI engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A Vauxhall Corsa 1.5 BlueHDI engine replacement costs £2,500-£4,000 supply-only for a rebuilt unit (DV5RC), with used engines from £500-£1,200. Fitting adds approximately £520-£780 in labour (8-12 hours). DPF and AdBlue system repairs are a more common (and cheaper) fix than full engine replacement on this engine.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of wet belt failure in a Vauxhall Corsa 1.2 PureTech?

acceptedAnswer.text: Common signs include a rattling noise from the timing cover on cold start, oil pressure warning light flashing, poor engine performance, and in severe cases, complete engine seizure. The 1.2 PureTech wet belt should be inspected at every service and replaced preventatively at 60,000 miles or 6 years. Stellantis has acknowledged excessive oil consumption and premature timing belt degradation on these engines.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of DPF or AdBlue failure in a Vauxhall Corsa 1.5 BlueHDI?

acceptedAnswer.text: Common signs include a DPF or check engine warning light, reduced power and sluggish performance, and in severe cases, the car may not start. AdBlue system failures can trigger warnings even when the tank is full, with possible causes including a faulty sensor, clogged injector, or bad pump. The 1.5 BlueHDI has been reported to suffer from injection system jams, mass air flow failure and AdBlue tank seizure.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Vauxhall Corsa 1.2 PureTech or 1.5 BlueHDI?

acceptedAnswer.text: For a 2019-2022 Corsa worth £6,000-£12,000, a rebuilt engine at £1,500-£4,000 plus fitting may represent 25-50% of the vehicle's value. For newer Corsa F (2023+) worth £12,000-£18,000, replacement is almost always viable. For higher-mileage Corsa F (2019-2021) with values under £7,000, a used engine may be more cost-effective than a rebuilt unit.

mainEntity.name: Can I replace a 1.2 PureTech engine with a different engine code?

acceptedAnswer.text: The EB2ADTS, EB2DTS and EB2FAD are all 1.2 PureTech engines with different power outputs (75PS, 100PS, 130PS). While physically similar, the ECU mapping, turbocharger and emissions hardware differ between power levels. A swap between 1.2 PureTech variants requires professional ECU reprogramming and may affect insurance. Always confirm compatibility with your specialist before purchasing. 1.5 BlueHDI diesel cannot be swapped into a petrol Corsa without extensive modifications.

historyTimeline.h2: Vauxhall Corsa 1.2 PureTech / 1.5 BlueHDI - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The sixth-generation Vauxhall Corsa F (2019-present) marked a significant shift for the UK's best-selling supermini, adopting PSA-developed engines following the brand's integration into the Stellantis group. The 1.2 PureTech petrol three-cylinder and 1.5 BlueHDI diesel four-cylinder replaced older GM-sourced Ecotec and CDTI units, bringing improved efficiency, lower emissions and stronger torque delivery. Both engines are also fitted to the Corsa Electric's petrol-engined stablemates.

milestones.description: Corsa F launched with 1.2 PureTech petrol (EB2ADTS, 100-130PS) and 1.5 BlueHDI diesel (DV5RC, 102PS)

Engine line-up updated with mild-hybrid 1.2 PureTech (EB2ADTD) and revised 1.5 BlueHDI (DV5RCf) for Euro 6d emissions compliance

commonProblems.h2: Vauxhall Corsa 1.2 PureTech / 1.5 BlueHDI Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Vauxhall Corsa 1.2 PureTech and 1.5 BlueHDI represent modern, efficient engine designs - but both have well-documented failure patterns. Petrol PureTech owners face wet belt degradation and oil starvation, while diesel BlueHDI owners contend with DPF clogging and AdBlue system failures. Rebuilt Corsa 1.2 PureTech and 1.5 BlueHDI engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing the original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: 1.2 PureTech Wet Belt Degradation - Why the Vauxhall Corsa 1.2 PureTech Fails Prematurely
problems.rootCause: The 1.2 PureTech engine uses a timing belt that runs in engine oil (a "wet belt"). Over time, the belt degrades and sheds rubber particles into the oil system.This clogs the oil pickup strainer and solenoids of the variable valve control.The resulting oil starvation leads to turbo failure, timing jump or complete engine seizure.Stellantis has acknowledged excessive oil consumption and premature timing belt degradation on these engines, offering customer support for repair expenses incurred between 2022 and 2024.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace timing belt, tensioner and oil pump belt; clean oil pickup and strainer
repairOptions.longevity: Recommended every 6 years or 60,000 miles - cheapest option
When belt has failed and caused oil starvation damage

problems.recommendation: For 1.2 PureTech owners, preventative wet belt replacement at 60,000 miles or 6 years is the most cost-effective approach - it costs a fraction of a full engine replacement. For 1.5 BlueHDI owners, regular motorway driving to allow DPF regeneration and using the correct AdBlue specification will extend component life. If the car is a higher-mileage Corsa F (2019-2021) worth under £7,000, a used engine may be more economically sensible than a rebuilt unit.

problems.h4: 1.5 BlueHDI DPF & AdBlue System Issues - Vauxhall Corsa 1.5 Diesel Problems
problems.rootCause: The 1.5 BlueHDI's DPF does not regenerate properly if the car is mainly used for short urban journeys.A clogged DPF causes the engine to go into limp mode and can prevent the car from starting.AdBlue system components (NOx sensors, heater, injector, tank) can fail, with the 1.5 BlueHDI reported to suffer from injection system jams, mass air flow failure and AdBlue tank seizure.AdBlue crystallisation at low temperatures can also block the injector.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Diagnostic forced regen or chemical clean
repairOptions.longevity: If DPF is partially blocked and no permanent damage
If DPF is blocked beyond cleaning or physically damaged

repairOptions.tier: AdBlue system repair (sensor / heater / injector / tank)
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace faulty NOx sensor, heater, injector or tank
repairOptions.longevity: If emissions warning light is active and AdBlue system flagged
When DPF/AdBlue issues have caused secondary turbo or EGR damage
